name: Old Town of Galle and its Fortifications
description: On Sri Lanka's southwestern coast, Galle's old town sits inside thick stone ramparts that jut out into the Indian Ocean. The Portuguese founded it in the 16th century, and the Dutch fortified it heavily from 1649, creating the largest surviving European-built fortress in Asia. You can walk the walls at sunset, then wander lanes of old colonial houses, churches and a cricket ground beside the sea.
